pipeline.value: Five text sources compared; PaddleOCR selected
Sentence embeddings and TF-IDF both scored macro F1 0.60 on the final test

types.name: Medical, first aid and workers' compensation
Issue ads, programs and corporate image
Legal memos, opinions and privileged letters

timing.stage: OCR, vision model (hard pages only, spread over all)
RAG suggestion (pages to a person only, spread over all)

decisions.decision: Classify from the record keeper's perspective
decisions.why: The same page can belong to different departments in different organizations.

decisions.decision: Five-fold cross-validation
decisions.why: Too few labels per department for a fixed test set.

decisions.decision: Build the categories from Philip Morris's departments
decisions.why: Ground the labels in how the client filed its records.

decisions.decision: Score at the department level
decisions.why: Measure whether a record reaches the right office of record. For model scoring, Administration is merged into Legal; the charts of manual labels keep the original departments.

decisions.decision: Run OCR on every pilot page
decisions.why: Embeddings and scan-quality tests need text for every page.

decisions.decision: Fix page rotation by keeping the more confident reading
decisions.why: The orientation check alone turned 18% of pages the wrong way.

decisions.decision: Restrict sampling to Philip Morris records
decisions.why: The benchmark pilot mixed several companies; the taxonomy is Philip Morris's.

decisions.decision: Freeze taxonomy v3: 8 departments, 55 record types
decisions.why: Capture the finest detail at labeling; types can be merged later.

decisions.decision: Raise the target to 250 if a department projects under 15
decisions.why: Class balance decides the label count, declared in advance.

decisions.decision: Keep Bates numbers and archive metadata out of the models
decisions.why: They can reveal the department and inflate scores.

decisions.decision: Label to 250 after the 50-label checkpoint
decisions.why: Quality, Finance and HR projected under 15 at 200; their handling is decided by counts at the end of labeling.

decisions.decision: Human resources out of scope for this project
decisions.why: Only 2 of the 262 reviewed documents belonged to it, too few to model; both were excluded with a recorded reason.

decisions.decision: Leave out pages that failed to download
decisions.why: Two documents in the labeled range returned a web page instead of the scan, so they were never seen. They are recorded as not retrieved, not as reviewed or excluded.

decisions.decision: Train and validate on the 250 labels; test on fresh pages
decisions.why: Five-fold cross-validation on the labels; 1,000 new documents are filed by the finished model, and a blind-labeled set of them forms the final test (size set by D-48).

decisions.decision: Establish a pool of 400 pages for labeling
decisions.why: Three downloads failed, so three replacements were drawn; the 1,000-document scale batch follows them.

decisions.decision: Keep the original PDFs and every archive field
decisions.why: The first download kept only a reduced image of each first page. All documents were fetched again by ID; the original record is kept and working images are made from it.

decisions.decision: Compare five text sources (four OCR runs and the archive's own text layer) before building the classifier
decisions.why: The project depends on reading the pages well, and the first engine had been a default nobody compared.

decisions.decision: Group pages by scan quality from the image alone
decisions.why: Different scan problems need different fixes; the groups were found before any OCR ran.

decisions.decision: Keep the file number in the OCR text, but not in what the classifier reads
decisions.why: Reading the file number is a real records capability; letting the model use a litigation stamp to decide the department would be a shortcut.

decisions.decision: Accept the sampling rules as they ran
decisions.why: A code audit checked the draw: it was proportional to the archive, and the duplicate rule keeps every sampled document distinct.

decisions.decision: Final test of 150 blind labels
decisions.why: A larger test gives a tighter estimate of how well the system files pages it has never seen.

decisions.decision: Test OCR on 22 pages, at least 4 of each kind of scan
decisions.why: A first check on mostly clean pages flattered one engine; every engine had to be judged on hard pages too.

decisions.decision: Save the position of every word read
decisions.why: The layout question needs to know where words sit on the page.

decisions.decision: Treat the archive's own text as a reference, not a candidate
decisions.why: A client's new scans would not come with an archive's text layer, so it shows whether local OCR is worth running but cannot be chosen.

decisions.decision: PaddleOCR is the reading engine
decisions.why: Chosen by the winning rule set before results: it found the most words correctly on forms with known text, and it is the only top engine that also gives each word's position and a confidence score, at under a second per page.

decisions.decision: Choose the text the classifier reads by how well it files
decisions.why: Each engine is strongest on different pages, so four versions of the text are compared on filing accuracy and the best one is used.

decisions.decision: Classify each document from its first page
decisions.why: It matches how every labeled page was judged, from the first page only; whole-document classification is future work.

decisions.decision: Re-fetch the archive's metadata, every field under its own name
decisions.why: The first download shifted values into the wrong columns (e.g. box); found before any result used it.

decisions.decision: Fix the five folds once: departments balanced, archive boxes kept together
decisions.why: Every model is scored on the same split, and a page is never tested against a near-copy from its own box.

decisions.decision: The classifier reads the hybrid text
decisions.why: It scored highest by the rule set in advance, effectively tied with PaddleOCR alone.

decisions.decision: File automatically only at 90% expected accuracy
decisions.why: A records standard set before any routing result; the cutoff is chosen on training folds only.

decisions.decision: Represent each page by its meaning with a local embedding model
decisions.why: Word counts missed pages whose purpose differs from their topic; meaning raised macro F1 from 0.56 to 0.68.

decisions.decision: Review suggestions come from a small local language model (Qwen3 8B)
decisions.why: It runs on the same PC, so pages never leave the machine; one model is kept frozen for the evaluation.

decisions.decision: Judge the suggestion against the classifier's own first choice, with and without its hints
decisions.why: A rule set before results: the suggestion must be right more often than the classifier on the pages a person reviews.

decisions.decision: Freeze the whole pipeline before the final test
decisions.why: Every setting was written down before a single test page was predicted, including the 0.55 cutoff (chosen on the pooled cross-validated predictions), so the final numbers could not be tuned to the test.

decisions.decision: Score the 150 held-back pages once and report what fell short
decisions.why: Auto-filing reached 87% against a 90% target, and meaning tied word counts on new pages; both are findings, and nothing was changed after scoring.

decisions.decision: Run the frozen pipeline on 1,000 new pages
decisions.why: Answers the client's practical question: how much is filed alone, how much reaches a person, and how long it takes.
